name: Compare folders
description: What is only on one side, and what is on both but different. The two panels are the two sides.

name: Disk map
description: What is taking up the room: a ring of folders you can walk into, mark, and have the application clear away.

name: Find duplicates
description: The same file kept in more than one place: sets of identical copies under a folder, biggest first, with what the extra copies are costing.

name: FBX
description: Shows an FBX: the model, shaded and turnable, playing its animation; and what the file holds — meshes, skeleton, clips and how long they run.

name: FTP
description: Browse and transfer over FTP. Set up connections from Drives and connections.

name: Git
description: The repository the panel is standing in, on one page: its branches, its log with the shape of the history drawn, what each commit touched and the difference itself.

name: Images
description: Displays raster images, zoomable and pannable.

name: Node graphs
description: Files that are a node graph, drawn as one: a ComfyUI workflow with its prompts and seeds on the boxes, the API export the server is sent, an n8n export with its sticky notes and the agents' tools, and Node-RED flows, Godot scenes with a frame per tab. Shift+F3 on a .json.

name: SMB
description: Browse and transfer over SMB2. Set up connections from Drives and connections.

name: System information
description: What this machine is: operating system, processor, memory, graphics and disks.

name: Files as text
description: One viewer for the files that are text: plain, coloured by language, formatted JSON, Markdown, delimited tables, numbered lines, and the hex dump nothing else claims. Shift+F3 chooses between the readings.

name: Web resources
description: Opens a web page as a folder of the things it is made of — images, scripts, stylesheets, and the pages it links to. Read and copy; nothing is ever written back.

name: Archives
description: Opens ZIP archives as folders, and lists their contents with F3. An example of work that needs real code, not a declarative render spec.
